metadata.title: Nvidia drops to No. 3, as its market cap is set to fall below Microsoft’s - MarketWatch

content.text:
1 hour ago
Nvidia drops to No. 3, as its market cap is set to fall below Microsoft’s
In a little over a week, a one-man scandal has knocked Nvidia off its perch as the most valuable company down to third, as the chip giant has lost more than a trillion dollars of market capitalization.
Nvidia's stock was sinking 8.5% in premarket trading and Microsoft's stock was down 0.4%. Nvidia has 24.1 billion shares outstanding and Microsoft has 7.43 billion shares outstanding, based on the companies' latest quarterly filings. At current implied premarket prices, Nvidia's market cap would be $3.832 trillion and Microsoft's would be $3.854 trillion.
The last time Nvidia was No. 1 was Nov. 3, when it closed with a market cap of $4.991 trillion and Apple's was $4.823 trillion, according to FactSet data. The next rung on the ladder is Alphabet in fourth place, with a current market cap of about $3.58 trillion.
